name: manual_45e77b
claim: Python's stdlib ipaddress.IPv4Address.is_global returning True for every multicast address (including the 224.0.0.0/4 network base itself) was confirmed on CPython 3.13.0 specifically -- this repo's declared floor is >=3.11, and CPython 3.13 changed other ipaddress edge-case classifications, so this exact claim is untested below 3.13 and should be re-verified if it becomes load-bearing on an older interpreter
conditions: declared python floor vs confirmed version

decisions.notes: Supersedes lesson_a045e9f02292 (CodeRabbit review #4989313231 on PT PR #359, finding on .agent/memory/candidates/graduated/a045e9f02292.json): the original claim stated the is_global/multicast behavior as universal without naming which Python version it was confirmed against, while pyproject.toml declares requires-python >=3.11 and mypy pins python_version=3.11 -- a 2-version gap between 'confirmed on' and 'declared floor'. Version-qualifying doesn't change the fix (the test oracle correctly uses 'not is_global or is_multicast' regardless of version), but an unqualified universal claim in memory is a liability if a future session runs on an older interpreter and assumes the same behavior without re-checking. Also updated the inline comment in tests/test_ssrf_fetch_policy.py to carry the same qualification.
